# Tally: implementation plan for the final version

Written 10 Oct 2026, 21:05 IST, updated 21:20 IST against `main` at `7f37c0e`. Submission closes 12 Oct, 23:55 IST. This plan replaces sections 2 and 5 to 8 of the first plan (`neatlogs-hack-1/tally-implementation-plan.md`); the product idea and the routing rule in that plan still stand.

Everything in this document is still to be built unless it is listed under "Built" in section 1.

## 1. Where we start from

### Built and on `main` (19 PRs merged, 184 tests passing)

- **One run loop.** Intake, sizing, routing, ceiling watcher, test verification, one escalation, ledger. A dry run uses the same loop with only the worker faked.
- **CFO agent.** Sizer, price history with a no-data prior, routing rule with budget check and a one-sentence reason, ceiling watcher, escalation, baseline mode.
- **Adapters.** Agent Orchestrator (spawn, poll, usage, kill), GitHub issue intake with a YAML fallback, test verifier, neatlogs trace, entire-graph sizing, file price history, cfo.ai budget.
- **CLI.** `tally run` (`--dry-run`, `--plan`, `--only`, `--budget`, `--baseline`), `tally demo` (and `--live`, with all three products on and no real workers), `tally dashboard`, `tally doctor`, `tally login cfoai`.
- **Dashboard.** Static page: budget bar, integrations strip, Tasks (one row per piece of work), Ledger (one row per paid attempt), sample and replay modes.
- **Accounts.** neatlogs key set, Entire logged in with the repo copied to project `neatlogs-hack`, cfo.ai logged in with a budget table that Tally has read live ($40 for October).

### Not yet true

- **No real worker has ever run.** Every cost seen so far is simulated. This is the last piece of V1 and it needs your go-ahead.
- **cfo.ai write-back** has only been tested against a fake server.
- **Ledger rows have a neatlogs trace id but no clickable link.** The address format of a trace in the neatlogs dashboard has not been verified.
- **Entire records none of the Codex workers.** Their hooks are waiting for your approval (`/hooks` in Codex).
- **neatlogs sees decisions, not worker sessions.** The worker hook packages are not installed.
- **The cheap-tier threshold (0.65) is fitted to the sample backlog**, not measured.

## 2. What the final version is

A judge can do three things, and each one works without help:

1. Open a public dashboard and see real recorded runs: what each task cost, why it went to that model, what was stopped, what was escalated, and how the total compares with sending everything to the top model.
2. Run `tally demo` on their own machine with no accounts and watch the full loop in two minutes.
3. Run `tally init` in their own repository and have Tally drive their agents on their issues.

Behind that sits one backend, used by all three, and five outside products that each make a decision possible at run time.

| Judged on | Weight | What the final version shows |
|---|---|---|
| The agent | 30% | Real runs on a real backlog, measured against a baseline, with a stopped runaway and a recovered failure. |
| Use of neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai | 25% | Each product changes a decision during the run (section 4), and the dashboard links to the evidence. |
| Demo video | 20% | The dashboard tells the story on real data. |
| Building in public | 15% | #neatHack posts with dashboard screenshots and real numbers. |
| Usefulness and originality | 10% | "They cap people, we cap tasks", backed by the experiment and a business plan in cfo.ai. |

## 3. Backend

| # | Work | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | **First real run.** Register fly-doom-jev as an AO project, run one task with a small budget. | A worker opens a PR, the tests decide the result, one ledger row has real tokens and cost. |
| B2 | **Forced failure and handoff.** Run one medium task with a ceiling set far too low. | The worker is stopped at the ceiling, and a stronger model continues on the same branch from the handoff summary and finishes. |
| B3 | **Worker setup per task.** Each worker checkout needs `make setup` (about a minute, 450 MB). Run it before the worker starts and keep its cost out of the task's ceiling. | A real task does not fail or get stopped because of environment setup. |
| B4 | **Concurrency.** Up to three workers at once, with the budget check done before each spawn so parallel tasks cannot overspend together. | A seven-task run with three in flight never exceeds the budget. |
| B5 | **Resume and partial failure.** Kill Tally mid-run and restart. | No finished task is redone and no cost is counted twice, including while workers are still alive. |
| B6 | **Model tiers.** Subscription tiers through `ao spawn` by default. Gateway tiers (paid per token) if you approve where the key lives (section 10). | `tally.yaml` can mix both, and every tier's cost is tokens times list price. |
| B7 | **Routing from history.** Replace the fixed prior with real cost and pass rate per task size and model from earlier runs. Recompute the cheap threshold from that data. | After two runs, at least one routing decision cites history, and the threshold is no longer the hand-set 0.65. |
| B8 | **Experiment runner.** `tally experiment --repeats N` runs baseline and Tally modes from the same starting commit and writes a report. | Report shows cost per merged PR, pass rate, total cost and spread, per mode. |
| B9 | **Setup wizard.** `tally init` detects the test command, asks for a budget and issue label, connects each product, writes `tally.yaml`. | A second repository goes from nothing to one finished task using only the README. |
| B10 | **Each product optional.** Run with each of neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai off in turn. | The run completes and the dashboard says exactly what was off and what replaced it. |
| B11 | **Housekeeping.** Fix the 14 npm audit findings without breaking changes, replace your cfo.ai workspace id in the public demo config with a placeholder, install `tally` on PATH (`npm link`). | `npm audit` shows no high findings; no personal ids in the repo. |

## 4. The five products

### neatlogs

| # | Work | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| N1 | Clickable trace link on every ledger row. The trace id and one neatlogs session per run are done; the link needs the real address format of a trace. | Clicking a dashboard row opens its decision trace. |
| N2 | Worker session traces: install the neatlogs hooks for Claude Code and Codex, and tag each worker session with its Tally task id. | A failed worker's trace shows where it failed, next to the CFO decision that sent it there. |
| N3 | Read history back from neatlogs (cost and outcome per past run) to feed B7. Needs a service-account token from you. | Routing history comes from neatlogs; the local file remains the fallback. |
| N4 | Two labelled trace sets, baseline and Tally, for the experiment. | The comparison numbers in the report can each be traced to a neatlogs trace. |

### Entire: graph

| # | Work | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | Real sizing on the target repository: search on the issue text, impact on the top symbols, count files, callers and co-change files. Already checked once by hand. | Each real task's "why" sentence cites numbers that came from the graph. |
| E2 | Verdict from `entire graph verify`: which tests newly pass or fail against a baseline, in place of a bare exit code. | A task that breaks an unrelated test is marked failed with the test named. |
| E3 | Impact shown on the dashboard: files touched and dependents per task. | Visible on each task row. |

### Entire: brain

I am reading "brain" as Entire's memory of agent work: checkpoints, session transcripts, semantic search over them, recaps and handoff. The Entire CLI has no feature called "brain", so tell me if you mean something else.

| # | Work | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| E4 | Capture: approve the Codex hooks so every worker session becomes a checkpoint. | `entire checkpoint list` shows the worker sessions of a real run. |
| E5 | Handoff: on escalation, pass the failed attempt's checkpoint summary and branch to the stronger model. The summary call spends tokens, so it goes in the ledger as its own line. | B2 passes using a real summary. |
| E6 | Recall before routing: search past checkpoints for work on the same files, and let a previous failure on that area lower confidence. | A routing reason reads "a cheap attempt failed on this area before". |
| E7 | Checkpoint id and link on every ledger row. | Clicking a row opens the worker's session on Entire. |
| E8 | Keep the Entire copy current: push branches and checkpoints after each merge and each run. | Entire shows the same head commit as GitHub. |

### cfo.ai

| # | Work | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | Live write-back in a real run. | "Agent spend" in your workspace equals the ledger total of real attempts. |
| C2 | Dry runs read the live budget and never write. Done. | `tally demo --live` shows cfo.ai on, budget from cfo.ai. |
| C3 | Budget by period: Tally respects the month's remaining budget across runs, not only one run's limit. | A run started with $3 remaining stops at $3. |
| C4 | Spend detail in cfo.ai: a table by model tier and by run, so the finance view answers "where did it go". | The cfo.ai page matches the dashboard's ledger totals. |
| C5 | Business plan in cfo.ai: pricing, costs, revenue, runway, fed by the market size from CrustData. I build this from this session through the cfo.ai connection, with your pricing assumptions. | A shareable plan page exists. |

### CrustData

| # | Work | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Spike: confirm what the API returns for a company search with the key you have. Nothing has been tested yet. | A short findings note. |
| D2 | `tally market`: search for engineering teams adopting coding agents, save the list and the query. | The search can be rerun and returns the same kind of result. |
| D3 | Market size into the cfo.ai business plan (C5). | The plan's market row cites the CrustData list. |

### Agent Orchestrator

Tally already uses AO to spawn, watch, meter and stop workers. One addition:

| # | Work | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | Session link on every ledger row, and the worker's harness and model as AO reports them. | A row links to the AO session that did the work. |

## 5. Frontend dashboard

The dashboard stays a static page with no framework. That is what lets the same files run locally and on AWS with no server.

| # | Work | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| F1 | **Evidence links** on each ledger row: PR, neatlogs trace, Entire checkpoint, AO session. | All four open from a real run's row. |
| F2 | **Live view**: tasks appear as running, with cost climbing toward the ceiling, while a real run is in progress. | Watching a real run needs no refresh. |
| F3 | **Comparison view**: baseline against Tally for the same backlog, with cost per merged PR, pass rate, total, and spread across repeats. | The experiment report is readable on the page. |
| F4 | **Run picker**: choose among recorded runs. | The hosted page can show every published run. |
| F5 | **Impact and history** per task: graph numbers (E3) and whether history changed the decision (B7, E6). | Visible on the task row. |
| F6 | **Budget from cfo.ai**: the budget bar names its source and links to the cfo.ai table. | Matches the cfo.ai page. |
| F7 | **Honest labelling**: simulated, sample, real, and which products were off, on every view. | No view can be mistaken for a real run when it is not. |
| F8 | **Phone width and print**: readable on a phone, and the ledger prints cleanly. | Checked at 390 px wide. |

## 6. AWS, at the very end

| # | Work | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| H1 | Install the AWS CLI and confirm the keys in `~/.tally/.env` work. Not installed today. | `aws sts get-caller-identity` succeeds. |
| H2 | `tally publish`: upload the dashboard and the recorded run folders to an S3 bucket behind CloudFront. Read-only, no secrets, no run folder that contains keys or transcripts. | A public URL shows the final runs. |
| H3 | Tear-down command and a cost note. | One command removes everything. |

Nothing is deployed before the final runs exist, so that what is published is the real result. Creating public AWS resources waits for your go-ahead.

## 7. Who builds what

Three AO workers, one per lane, as now. Each lane owns its folders. I test every batch of PRs together before merging.

| Lane | Session | Final work |
|---|---|---|
| A: engine | `neatlogs-hack-2` | B1 to B6, B8, B9, B11, A1, H1 to H3 |
| B: agent and integrations | `neatlogs-hack-5` | B7, B10, N1 to N4, E1, E2, E5, E6, C1 to C4, D1, D2 |
| C: dashboard | `neatlogs-hack-6` | F1 to F8, E3, the fly-doom-jev backlog, the README quickstart |
| Orchestrator (this session) | | Merging, checking, C5 and D3 in cfo.ai, E8, this plan |

Tally's own real runs also spawn up to three AO workers. Real runs and the experiment are therefore scheduled when the lanes are quiet, so subscription limits are not hit from both sides.

## 8. The experiment

- **Backlog:** seven tasks on fly-doom-jev: three small, three medium, one that looks medium but is hard. Drafted, not yet filed.
- **Before:** every task on the top model, no ceilings.
- **After:** the same tasks routed by Tally.
- **Repeats:** two of each, three if time allows. Each run starts from the same commit.
- **Reported:** cost per merged PR, pass rate, total cost, and the spread. Every run is published, including any Tally loses.
- **Size:** 28 task runs, three at a time, roughly three to four hours including setup per worker.

## 9. Acceptance checks

Run in this order. Do not start a check until the one before it passes.

| # | Check | Pass when |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | `npm test`, typecheck, build | All clean on `main`. |
| T2 | `tally demo` and `tally demo --live` | Seven tasks; one stopped and recovered; the live variant shows all three products on with honest status. |
| T3 | One real task | PR opened, tests decide, ledger row real, trace in neatlogs, checkpoint in Entire, spend in cfo.ai. |
| T4 | Forced failure | Stopped at the ceiling, continued by a stronger model from the handoff, finished. |
| T5 | Budget too small | Tally completes what it can, marks the rest "not started: no budget", stays under budget. |
| T6 | Unsolvable task | Fails on both models, the run finishes the others. |
| T7 | Interrupted run | Resumes without redoing work or double counting. |
| T8 | Full run | Ledger total equals the sum of rows and equals cfo.ai. |
| T9 | Experiment | Both modes reported with spread; every number traceable to a neatlogs trace. |
| T10 | Stranger install | A person who has not seen the code completes one task on a second repository using only the README. |
| T11 | Products off | Each of the three off in turn; the run completes and says so. |
| T12 | Hosted page | Public URL loads on a phone, shows the final runs, exposes no keys. |

## 10. What only you can do

| Needed | For | Needed before |
|---|---|---|
| Go-ahead for the first real run on fly-doom-jev | B1, and everything after it | Anything else |
| Approve the Codex hooks (`/hooks` in Codex) | E4: without it Entire has no worker sessions | B1 |
| Say yes or no to installing the neatlogs worker hooks, which edit `~/.claude` and `~/.codex` | N2 | N2 |
| Go-ahead to file the seven issues on fly-doom-jev | Intake from GitHub issues; the YAML file works without it | The full seven-task run |
| Decide where the gateway key may live: in an AO project's settings, or behind a small local proxy Tally runs | B6: real per-token billing in the ledger. Without it, cost is tokens times list price on subscription models, and the video says so. | B6 |
| A neatlogs service-account token and project id | N3 | N3 |
| Your pricing assumptions for the business plan | C5 | C5 |
| Go-ahead to create public AWS resources, and install the AWS CLI | H1, H2 | H1 |
| #neatHack posts, and recording the video | 15% and 20% of the score | Submission |

## 11. Risks, and what gets cut first

- **Time.** The list is long for the time left before the 12 Oct, 23:55 IST deadline. If it slips, cut in this order: Slack alert (not planned above), E6, C4, F8, B9's wizard prompts (keep a hand-written `tally.yaml`), a third repeat, N3 (keep the local history file), H3. Never cut B1, B2, the baseline comparison, or the evidence links: each is named evidence.
- **Subscription limits.** Lanes and real runs share the same Claude and Codex plans. A limit hit mid-experiment pauses workers. The gateway tiers are the relief, which is why that decision matters.
- **Routing may save less than hoped.** The 20% cap bounds the loss per task. The result is published either way.
- **The failure scene may not happen by itself.** B2 produces it on purpose, and the video says so.
- **Entire handoff across models** worked once on a toy repository and has not been tried on a long session.
- **CrustData is untested.** If the API does not give a usable list, the market size in the plan is entered by hand and labelled as an estimate.
- **Environment setup per worker** on fly-doom-jev may dominate small tasks. B3 keeps it out of the ceiling, but it still costs wall-clock time in the experiment.

# Tally: implementation plan for the final version

Written 10 Oct 2026, 21:05 IST, updated 21:20 IST against `main` at `7f37c0e`. Submission closes 12 Oct, 23:55 IST. This plan replaces sections 2 and 5 to 8 of the first plan (`neatlogs-hack-1/tally-implementation-plan.md`); the product idea and the routing rule in that plan still stand.

Everything in this document is still to be built unless it is listed under "Built" in section 1.

## 1. Where we start from

### Built and on `main` (19 PRs merged, 184 tests passing)

- **One run loop.** Intake, sizing, routing, ceiling watcher, test verification, one escalation, ledger. A dry run uses the same loop with only the worker faked.
- **CFO agent.** Sizer, price history with a no-data prior, routing rule with budget check and a one-sentence reason, ceiling watcher, escalation, baseline mode.
- **Adapters.** Agent Orchestrator (spawn, poll, usage, kill), GitHub issue intake with a YAML fallback, test verifier, neatlogs trace, entire-graph sizing, file price history, cfo.ai budget.
- **CLI.** `tally run` (`--dry-run`, `--plan`, `--only`, `--budget`, `--baseline`), `tally demo` (and `--live`, with all three products on and no real workers), `tally dashboard`, `tally doctor`, `tally login cfoai`.
- **Dashboard.** Static page: budget bar, integrations strip, Tasks (one row per piece of work), Ledger (one row per paid attempt), sample and replay modes.
- **Accounts.** neatlogs key set, Entire logged in with the repo copied to project `neatlogs-hack`, cfo.ai logged in with a budget table that Tally has read live ($40 for October).

### Not yet true

- **No real worker has ever run.** Every cost seen so far is simulated. This is the last piece of V1 and it needs your go-ahead.
- **cfo.ai write-back** has only been tested against a fake server.
- **Ledger rows have a neatlogs trace id but no clickable link.** The address format of a trace in the neatlogs dashboard has not been verified.
- **Entire records none of the Codex workers.** Their hooks are waiting for your approval (`/hooks` in Codex).
- **neatlogs sees decisions, not worker sessions.** The worker hook packages are not installed.
- **The cheap-tier threshold (0.65) is fitted to the sample backlog**, not measured.

## 2. What the final version is

A judge can do three things, and each one works without help:

1. Open a public dashboard and see real recorded runs: what each task cost, why it went to that model, what was stopped, what was escalated, and how the total compares with sending everything to the top model.
2. Run `tally demo` on their own machine with no accounts and watch the full loop in two minutes.
3. Run `tally init` in their own repository and have Tally drive their agents on their issues.

Behind that sits one backend, used by all three, and five outside products that each make a decision possible at run time.

| Judged on | Weight | What the final version shows |
|---|---|---|
| The agent | 30% | Real runs on a real backlog, measured against a baseline, with a stopped runaway and a recovered failure. |
| Use of neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai | 25% | Each product changes a decision during the run (section 4), and the dashboard links to the evidence. |
| Demo video | 20% | The dashboard tells the story on real data. |
| Building in public | 15% | #neatHack posts with dashboard screenshots and real numbers. |
| Usefulness and originality | 10% | "They cap people, we cap tasks", backed by the experiment and a business plan in cfo.ai. |

## 3. Backend

| # | Work | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | **First real run.** Register fly-doom-jev as an AO project, run one task with a small budget. | A worker opens a PR, the tests decide the result, one ledger row has real tokens and cost. |
| B2 | **Forced failure and handoff.** Run one medium task with a ceiling set far too low. | The worker is stopped at the ceiling, and a stronger model continues on the same branch from the handoff summary and finishes. |
| B3 | **Worker setup per task.** Each worker checkout needs `make setup` (about a minute, 450 MB). Run it before the worker starts and keep its cost out of the task's ceiling. | A real task does not fail or get stopped because of environment setup. |
| B4 | **Concurrency.** Up to three workers at once, with the budget check done before each spawn so parallel tasks cannot overspend together. | A seven-task run with three in flight never exceeds the budget. |
| B5 | **Resume and partial failure.** Kill Tally mid-run and restart. | No finished task is redone and no cost is counted twice, including while workers are still alive. |

content.text: The important live finding: current `tally.history.record` traces are visible in the public list, but their public detail has `spansCount: 0`, no input/attributes, and `/spans` is still `409 TRACE_PROCESSING`. That means the existing reader cannot extract size/tier/result/cost from today’s history traces. I’m fixing that by encoding the history observation in the trace name itself, because `traceName` is present in the public list response.

The important live finding: current `tally.history.record` traces are visible in the public list, but their public detail has `spansCount: 0`, no input/attributes, and `/spans` is still `409 TRACE_PROCESSING`. That means the existing reader cannot extract size/tier/result/cost from today’s history traces. I’m fixing that by encoding the history observation in the trace name itself, because `traceName` is present in the public list response.

# Tally: implementation plan for the final version

Written 10 Oct 2026, 21:05 IST, updated 21:20 IST against `main` at `7f37c0e`. Submission closes 12 Oct, 23:55 IST. This plan replaces sections 2 and 5 to 8 of the first plan (`neatlogs-hack-1/tally-implementation-plan.md`); the product idea and the routing rule in that plan still stand.

Everything in this document is still to be built unless it is listed under "Built" in section 1.

## 1. Where we start from

### Built and on `main` (19 PRs merged, 184 tests passing)

- **One run loop.** Intake, sizing, routing, ceiling watcher, test verification, one escalation, ledger. A dry run uses the same loop with only the worker faked.
- **CFO agent.** Sizer, price history with a no-data prior, routing rule with budget check and a one-sentence reason, ceiling watcher, escalation, baseline mode.
- **Adapters.** Agent Orchestrator (spawn, poll, usage, kill), GitHub issue intake with a YAML fallback, test verifier, neatlogs trace, entire-graph sizing, file price history, cfo.ai budget.
- **CLI.** `tally run` (`--dry-run`, `--plan`, `--only`, `--budget`, `--baseline`), `tally demo` (and `--live`, with all three products on and no real workers), `tally dashboard`, `tally doctor`, `tally login cfoai`.
- **Dashboard.** Static page: budget bar, integrations strip, Tasks (one row per piece of work), Ledger (one row per paid attempt), sample and replay modes.
- **Accounts.** neatlogs key set, Entire logged in with the repo copied to project `neatlogs-hack`, cfo.ai logged in with a budget table that Tally has read live ($40 for October).

### Not yet true

- **No real worker has ever run.** Every cost seen so far is simulated. This is the last piece of V1 and it needs your go-ahead.
- **cfo.ai write-back** has only been tested against a fake server.
- **Ledger rows have a neatlogs trace id but no clickable link.** The address format of a trace in the neatlogs dashboard has not been verified.
- **Entire records none of the Codex workers.** Their hooks are waiting for your approval (`/hooks` in Codex).
- **neatlogs sees decisions, not worker sessions.** The worker hook packages are not installed.
- **The cheap-tier threshold (0.65) is fitted to the sample backlog**, not measured.

## 2. What the final version is

A judge can do three things, and each one works without help:

1. Open a public dashboard and see real recorded runs: what each task cost, why it went to that model, what was stopped, what was escalated, and how the total compares with sending everything to the top model.
2. Run `tally demo` on their own machine with no accounts and watch the full loop in two minutes.
3. Run `tally init` in their own repository and have Tally drive their agents on their issues.

Behind that sits one backend, used by all three, and five outside products that each make a decision possible at run time.

| Judged on | Weight | What the final version shows |
|---|---|---|
| The agent | 30% | Real runs on a real backlog, measured against a baseline, with a stopped runaway and a recovered failure. |
| Use of neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai | 25% | Each product changes a decision during the run (section 4), and the dashboard links to the evidence. |
| Demo video | 20% | The dashboard tells the story on real data. |
| Building in public | 15% | #neatHack posts with dashboard screenshots and real numbers. |
| Usefulness and originality | 10% | "They cap people, we cap tasks", backed by the experiment and a business plan in cfo.ai. |

## 3. Backend

| # | Work | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | **First real run.** Register fly-doom-jev as an AO project, run one task with a small budget. | A worker opens a PR, the tests decide the result, one ledger row has real tokens and cost. |
| B2 | **Forced failure and handoff.** Run one medium task with a ceiling set far too low. | The worker is stopped at the ceiling, and a stronger model continues on the same branch from the handoff summary and finishes. |
| B3 | **Worker setup per task.** Each worker checkout needs `make setup` (about a minute, 450 MB). Run it before the worker starts and keep its cost out of the task's ceiling. | A real task does not fail or get stopped because of environment setup. |
| B4 | **Concurrency.** Up to three workers at once, with the budget check done before each spawn so parallel tasks cannot overspend together. | A seven-task run with three in flight never exceeds the budget. |
| B5 | **Resume and partial failure.** Kill Tally mid-run and restart. | No finished task is redone and no cost is counted twice, including while workers are still alive. |
| B6 | **Model tiers.** Subscription tiers through `ao spawn` by default. Gateway tiers (paid per token) if you approve where the key lives (section 10). | `tally.yaml` can mix both, and every tier's cost is tokens times list price. |
| B7 | **Routing from history.** Replace the fixed prior with real cost and pass rate per task size and model from earlier runs. Recompute the cheap threshold from that data. | After two runs, at least one routing decision cites history, and the threshold is no longer the hand-set 0.65. |
| B8 | **Experiment runner.** `tally experiment --repeats N` runs baseline and Tally modes from the same starting commit and writes a report. | Report shows cost per merged PR, pass rate, total cost and spread, per mode. |
| B9 | **Setup wizard.** `tally init` detects the test command, asks for a budget and issue label, connects each product, writes `tally.yaml`. | A second repository goes from nothing to one finished task using only the README. |
| B10 | **Each product optional.** Run with each of neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai off in turn. | The run completes and the dashboard says exactly what was off and what replaced it. |
| B11 | **Housekeeping.** Fix the 14 npm audit findings without breaking changes, replace your cfo.ai workspace id in the public demo config with a placeholder, install `tally` on PATH (`npm link`). | `npm audit` shows no high findings; no personal ids in the repo. |

| F6 | **Budget from cfo.ai**: the budget bar names its source and links to the cfo.ai table. | Matches the cfo.ai page. |
| F7 | **Honest labelling**: simulated, sample, real, and which products were off, on every view. | No view can be mistaken for a real run when it is not. |
| F8 | **Phone width and print**: readable on a phone, and the ledger prints cleanly. | Checked at 390 px wide. |

## 6. AWS, at the very end

| # | Work | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| H1 | Install the AWS CLI and confirm the keys in `~/.tally/.env` work. Not installed today. | `aws sts get-caller-identity` succeeds. |
| H2 | `tally publish`: upload the dashboard and the recorded run folders to an S3 bucket behind CloudFront. Read-only, no secrets, no run folder that contains keys or transcripts. | A public URL shows the final runs. |
| H3 | Tear-down command and a cost note. | One command removes everything. |

Nothing is deployed before the final runs exist, so that what is published is the real result. Creating public AWS resources waits for your go-ahead.

## 7. Who builds what

Three AO workers, one per lane, as now. Each lane owns its folders. I test every batch of PRs together before merging.

| Lane | Session | Final work |
|---|---|---|
| A: engine | `neatlogs-hack-2` | B1 to B6, B8, B9, B11, A1, H1 to H3 |
| B: agent and integrations | `neatlogs-hack-5` | B7, B10, N1 to N4, E1, E2, E5, E6, C1 to C4, D1, D2 |
| C: dashboard | `neatlogs-hack-6` | F1 to F8, E3, the fly-doom-jev backlog, the README quickstart |
| Orchestrator (this session) | | Merging, checking, C5 and D3 in cfo.ai, E8, this plan |

Tally's own real runs also spawn up to three AO workers. Real runs and the experiment are therefore scheduled when the lanes are quiet, so subscription limits are not hit from both sides.

## 8. The experiment

- **Backlog:** seven tasks on fly-doom-jev: three small, three medium, one that looks medium but is hard. Drafted, not yet filed.
- **Before:** every task on the top model, no ceilings.
- **After:** the same tasks routed by Tally.
- **Repeats:** two of each, three if time allows. Each run starts from the same commit.
- **Reported:** cost per merged PR, pass rate, total cost, and the spread. Every run is published, including any Tally loses.
- **Size:** 28 task runs, three at a time, roughly three to four hours including setup per worker.

## 9. Acceptance checks

Run in this order. Do not start a check until the one before it passes.

| # | Check | Pass when |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | `npm test`, typecheck, build | All clean on `main`. |
| T2 | `tally demo` and `tally demo --live` | Seven tasks; one stopped and recovered; the live variant shows all three products on with honest status. |
| T3 | One real task | PR opened, tests decide, ledger row real, trace in neatlogs, checkpoint in Entire, spend in cfo.ai. |
| T4 | Forced failure | Stopped at the ceiling, continued by a stronger model from the handoff, finished. |
| T5 | Budget too small | Tally completes what it can, marks the rest "not started: no budget", stays under budget. |
| T6 | Unsolvable task | Fails on both models, the run finishes the others. |
| T7 | Interrupted run | Resumes without redoing work or double counting. |
| T8 | Full run | Ledger total equals the sum of rows and equals cfo.ai. |
| T9 | Experiment | Both modes reported with spread; every number traceable to a neatlogs trace. |
| T10 | Stranger install | A person who has not seen the code completes one task on a second repository using only the README. |
| T11 | Products off | Each of the three off in turn; the run completes and says so. |
| T12 | Hosted page | Public URL loads on a phone, shows the final runs, exposes no keys. |

## 10. What only you can do

| Needed | For | Needed before |
|---|---|---|
| Go-ahead for the first real run on fly-doom-jev | B1, and everything after it | Anything else |
| Approve the Codex hooks (`/hooks` in Codex) | E4: without it Entire has no worker sessions | B1 |
| Say yes or no to installing the neatlogs worker hooks, which edit `~/.claude` and `~/.codex` | N2 | N2 |
| Go-ahead to file the seven issues on fly-doom-jev | Intake from GitHub issues; the YAML file works without it | The full seven-task run |
| Decide where the gateway key may live: in an AO project's settings, or behind a small local proxy Tally runs | B6: real per-token billing in the ledger. Without it, cost is tokens times list price on subscription models, and the video says so. | B6 |
| A neatlogs service-account token and project id | N3 | N3 |
| Your pricing assumptions for the business plan | C5 | C5 |
| Go-ahead to create public AWS resources, and install the AWS CLI | H1, H2 | H1 |
| #neatHack posts, and recording the video | 15% and 20% of the score | Submission |

## 11. Risks, and what gets cut first

- **Time.** The list is long for the time left before the 12 Oct, 23:55 IST deadline. If it slips, cut in this order: Slack alert (not planned above), E6, C4, F8, B9's wizard prompts (keep a hand-written `tally.yaml`), a third repeat, N3 (keep the local history file), H3. Never cut B1, B2, the baseline comparison, or the evidence links: each is named evidence.
- **Subscription limits.** Lanes and real runs share the same Claude and Codex plans. A limit hit mid-experiment pauses workers. The gateway tiers are the relief, which is why that decision matters.
- **Routing may save less than hoped.** The 20% cap bounds the loss per task. The result is published either way.
- **The failure scene may not happen by itself.** B2 produces it on purpose, and the video says so.
- **Entire handoff across models** worked once on a toy repository and has not been tried on a long session.
- **CrustData is untested.** If the API does not give a usable list, the market size in the plan is entered by hand and labelled as an estimate.
- **Environment setup per worker** on fly-doom-jev may dominate small tasks. B3 keeps it out of the ceiling, but it still costs wall-clock time in the experiment.

# Escalation Requests

Commands are run outside the sandbox if they are approved by the user, or match an existing rule that allows it to run unrestricted. The command string is split into independent command segments at shell control operators, including but not limited to:

- Pipes: |
- Logical operators: &&, ||

Each resulting segment is evaluated independently for sandbox restrictions and approval requirements.

["git", "pull"]

["tee", "output.txt"]

Commands that use more advanced shell features like redirection (>, >>, <), substitutions ($(...), ...), environment variables (FOO=bar), or wildcard patterns (*, ?) will not be evaluated against rules, to limit the scope of what an approved rule allows.

## How to request escalation

While commands are running inside the sandbox, here are some scenarios that will require escalation outside the sandbox:

- You need to run a command that writes to a directory that requires it (e.g. running tests that write to /var)

A plugin is a local bundle of skills, MCP servers, and apps.

- Skill naming: If a plugin contributes skills, those skill entries are prefixed with `plugin_name:` in the Skills list.

# Tally: implementation plan for the final version

Written 10 Oct 2026, 21:05 IST, updated 21:20 IST against `main` at `7f37c0e`. Submission closes 12 Oct, 23:55 IST. This plan replaces sections 2 and 5 to 8 of the first plan (`neatlogs-hack-1/tally-implementation-plan.md`); the product idea and the routing rule in that plan still stand.

Everything in this document is still to be built unless it is listed under "Built" in section 1.

## 1. Where we start from

### Built and on `main` (19 PRs merged, 184 tests passing)

- **One run loop.** Intake, sizing, routing, ceiling watcher, test verification, one escalation, ledger. A dry run uses the same loop with only the worker faked.
- **CFO agent.** Sizer, price history with a no-data prior, routing rule with budget check and a one-sentence reason, ceiling watcher, escalation, baseline mode.
- **Adapters.** Agent Orchestrator (spawn, poll, usage, kill), GitHub issue intake with a YAML fallback, test verifier, neatlogs trace, entire-graph sizing, file price history, cfo.ai budget.
- **CLI.** `tally run` (`--dry-run`, `--plan`, `--only`, `--budget`, `--baseline`), `tally demo` (and `--live`, with all three products on and no real workers), `tally dashboard`, `tally doctor`, `tally login cfoai`.
- **Dashboard.** Static page: budget bar, integrations strip, Tasks (one row per piece of work), Ledger (one row per paid attempt), sample and replay modes.
- **Accounts.** neatlogs key set, Entire logged in with the repo copied to project `neatlogs-hack`, cfo.ai logged in with a budget table that Tally has read live ($40 for October).

### Not yet true

- **No real worker has ever run.** Every cost seen so far is simulated. This is the last piece of V1 and it needs your go-ahead.
- **cfo.ai write-back** has only been tested against a fake server.
- **Ledger rows have a neatlogs trace id but no clickable link.** The address format of a trace in the neatlogs dashboard has not been verified.
- **Entire records none of the Codex workers.** Their hooks are waiting for your approval (`/hooks` in Codex).
- **neatlogs sees decisions, not worker sessions.** The worker hook packages are not installed.
- **The cheap-tier threshold (0.65) is fitted to the sample backlog**, not measured.

## 2. What the final version is

A judge can do three things, and each one works without help:

1. Open a public dashboard and see real recorded runs: what each task cost, why it went to that model, what was stopped, what was escalated, and how the total compares with sending everything to the top model.
2. Run `tally demo` on their own machine with no accounts and watch the full loop in two minutes.
3. Run `tally init` in their own repository and have Tally drive their agents on their issues.

Behind that sits one backend, used by all three, and five outside products that each make a decision possible at run time.

| Judged on | Weight | What the final version shows |
|---|---|---|
| The agent | 30% | Real runs on a real backlog, measured against a baseline, with a stopped runaway and a recovered failure. |
| Use of neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai | 25% | Each product changes a decision during the run (section 4), and the dashboard links to the evidence. |
| Demo video | 20% | The dashboard tells the story on real data. |
| Building in public | 15% | #neatHack posts with dashboard screenshots and real numbers. |
| Usefulness and originality | 10% | "They cap people, we cap tasks", backed by the experiment and a business plan in cfo.ai. |

## 3. Backend

| # | Work | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | **First real run.** Register fly-doom-jev as an AO project, run one task with a small budget. | A worker opens a PR, the tests decide the result, one ledger row has real tokens and cost. |
| B2 | **Forced failure and handoff.** Run one medium task with a ceiling set far too low. | The worker is stopped at the ceiling, and a stronger model continues on the same branch from the handoff summary and finishes. |
| B3 | **Worker setup per task.** Each worker checkout needs `make setup` (about a minute, 450 MB). Run it before the worker starts and keep its cost out of the task's ceiling. | A real task does not fail or get stopped because of environment setup. |
| B4 | **Concurrency.** Up to three workers at once, with the budget check done before each spawn so parallel tasks cannot overspend together. | A seven-task run with three in flight never exceeds the budget. |
| B5 | **Resume and partial failure.** Kill Tally mid-run and restart. | No finished task is redone and no cost is counted twice, including while workers are still alive. |
| B6 | **Model tiers.** Subscription tiers through `ao spawn` by default. Gateway tiers (paid per token) if you approve where the key lives (section 10). | `tally.yaml` can mix both, and every tier's cost is tokens times list price. |
| B7 | **Routing from history.** Replace the fixed prior with real cost and pass rate per task size and model from earlier runs. Recompute the cheap threshold from that data. | After two runs, at least one routing decision cites history, and the threshold is no longer the hand-set 0.65. |
| B8 | **Experiment runner.** `tally experiment --repeats N` runs baseline and Tally modes from the same starting commit and writes a report. | Report shows cost per merged PR, pass rate, total cost and spread, per mode. |
| B9 | **Setup wizard.** `tally init` detects the test command, asks for a budget and issue label, connects each product, writes `tally.yaml`. | A second repository goes from nothing to one finished task using only the README. |
| B10 | **Each product optional.** Run with each of neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai off in turn. | The run completes and the dashboard says exactly what was off and what replaced it. |
| B11 | **Housekeeping.** Fix the 14 npm audit findings without breaking changes, replace your cfo.ai workspace id in the public demo config with a placeholder, install `tally` on PATH (`npm link`). | `npm audit` shows no high findings; no personal ids in the repo. |

## 4. The five products

### neatlogs

| # | Work | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| N1 | Clickable trace link on every ledger row. The trace id and one neatlogs session per run are done; the link needs the real address format of a trace. | Clicking a dashboard row opens its decision trace. |
| N2 | Worker session traces: install the neatlogs hooks for Claude Code and Codex, and tag each worker session with its Tally task id. | A failed worker's trace shows where it failed, next to the CFO decision that sent it there. |
| N3 | Read history back from neatlogs (cost and outcome per past run) to feed B7. Needs a service-account token from you. | Routing history comes from neatlogs; the local file remains the fallback. |
| N4 | Two labelled trace sets, baseline and Tally, for the experiment. | The comparison numbers in the report can each be traced to a neatlogs trace. |

### Entire: graph

| # | Work | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | Real sizing on the target repository: search on the issue text, impact on the top symbols, count files, callers and co-change files. Already checked once by hand. | Each real task's "why" sentence cites numbers that came from the graph. |
| E2 | Verdict from `entire graph verify`: which tests newly pass or fail against a baseline, in place of a bare exit code. | A task that breaks an unrelated test is marked failed with the test named. |
| E3 | Impact shown on the dashboard: files touched and dependents per task. | Visible on each task row. |

### Entire: brain

I am reading "brain" as Entire's memory of agent work: checkpoints, session transcripts, semantic search over them, recaps and handoff. The Entire CLI has no feature called "brain", so tell me if you mean something else.

| # | Work | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| E4 | Capture: approve the Codex hooks so every worker session becomes a checkpoint. | `entire checkpoint list` shows the worker sessions of a real run. |
| E5 | Handoff: on escalation, pass the failed attempt's checkpoint summary and branch to the stronger model. The summary call spends tokens, so it goes in the ledger as its own line. | B2 passes using a real summary. |
| E6 | Recall before routing: search past checkpoints for work on the same files, and let a previous failure on that area lower confidence. | A routing reason reads "a cheap attempt failed on this area before". |
| E7 | Checkpoint id and link on every ledger row. | Clicking a row opens the worker's session on Entire. |
| E8 | Keep the Entire copy current: push branches and checkpoints after each merge and each run. | Entire shows the same head commit as GitHub. |

### cfo.ai

| # | Work | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | Live write-back in a real run. | "Agent spend" in your workspace equals the ledger total of real attempts. |
| C2 | Dry runs read the live budget and never write. Done. | `tally demo --live` shows cfo.ai on, budget from cfo.ai. |
| C3 | Budget by period: Tally respects the month's remaining budget across runs, not only one run's limit. | A run started with $3 remaining stops at $3. |
| C4 | Spend detail in cfo.ai: a table by model tier and by run, so the finance view answers "where did it go". | The cfo.ai page matches the dashboard's ledger totals. |
| C5 | Business plan in cfo.ai: pricing, costs, revenue, runway, fed by the market size from CrustData. I build this from this session through the cfo.ai connection, with your pricing assumptions. | A shareable plan page exists. |

### CrustData

| # | Work | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Spike: confirm what the API returns for a company search with the key you have. Nothing has been tested yet. | A short findings note. |
| D2 | `tally market`: search for engineering teams adopting coding agents, save the list and the query. | The search can be rerun and returns the same kind of result. |
| D3 | Market size into the cfo.ai business plan (C5). | The plan's market row cites the CrustData list. |

### Agent Orchestrator

Tally already uses AO to spawn, watch, meter and stop workers. One addition:

| # | Work | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | Session link on every ledger row, and the worker's harness and model as AO reports them. | A row links to the AO session that did the work. |

## 5. Frontend dashboard

The dashboard stays a static page with no framework. That is what lets the same files run locally and on AWS with no server.

| # | Work | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| F1 | **Evidence links** on each ledger row: PR, neatlogs trace, Entire checkpoint, AO session. | All four open from a real run's row. |
| F2 | **Live view**: tasks appear as running, with cost climbing toward the ceiling, while a real run is in progress. | Watching a real run needs no refresh. |
| F3 | **Comparison view**: baseline against Tally for the same backlog, with cost per merged PR, pass rate, total, and spread across repeats. | The experiment report is readable on the page. |
| F4 | **Run picker**: choose among recorded runs. | The hosted page can show every published run. |
| F5 | **Impact and history** per task: graph numbers (E3) and whether history changed the decision (B7, E6). | Visible on the task row. |
| F6 | **Budget from cfo.ai**: the budget bar names its source and links to the cfo.ai table. | Matches the cfo.ai page. |
| F7 | **Honest labelling**: simulated, sample, real, and which products were off, on every view. | No view can be mistaken for a real run when it is not. |
| F8 | **Phone width and print**: readable on a phone, and the ledger prints cleanly. | Checked at 390 px wide. |

## 6. AWS, at the very end

| # | Work | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| H1 | Find a working way to act as the hackathon AWS user. The CLI is installed, but the key lines in `~/.tally/.env` are empty and cannot be filled (see below). | An identity check succeeds somewhere: CloudShell, or the organisers' recommended route. |
| H2 | `tally publish`: upload the dashboard and the recorded run folders to an S3 bucket behind CloudFront. Read-only, no secrets, no run folder that contains keys or transcripts. | A public URL shows the final runs. |
| H3 | Tear-down command and a cost note. | One command removes everything. |

Nothing is deployed before the final runs exist, so that what is published is the real result. Creating public AWS resources waits for your go-ahead.

**Parked until the end, at your request (10 Oct).** What we learned about the account: it is a hackathon-issued IAM user (`hackathon-user-038`) under an organisation policy that explicitly denies creating access keys. `aws login` from the laptop returned 400, and CloudShell failed to start from the Global view (us-east-1 not yet tried). So Tally cannot deploy from the laptop with this account. H2 therefore changes: `tally publish` produces a ready-to-upload folder plus a short script, and the upload is done either in CloudShell or by hand in the AWS console (S3 static hosting, or Amplify Hosting with a dragged zip). Which services the account allows is unknown; ask the organisers.

## 7. Who builds what

Three AO workers, one per lane, as now. Each lane owns its folders. I test every batch of PRs together before merging.

| Lane | Session | Final work |
|---|---|---|
| A: engine | `neatlogs-hack-2` | B1 to B6, B8, B9, B11, A1, H1 to H3 |
| B: agent and integrations | `neatlogs-hack-5` | B7, B10, N1 to N4, E1, E2, E5, E6, C1 to C4, D1, D2 |
| C: dashboard | `neatlogs-hack-6` | F1 to F8, E3, the fly-doom-jev backlog, the README quickstart |
| Orchestrator (this session) | | Merging, checking, C5 and D3 in cfo.ai, E8, this plan |

Tally's own real runs also spawn up to three AO workers. Real runs and the experiment are therefore scheduled when the lanes are quiet, so subscription limits are not hit from both sides.

## 8. The experiment

- **Backlog:** seven tasks on fly-doom-jev: three small, three medium, one that looks medium but is hard. Drafted, not yet filed.
- **Before:** every task on the top model, no ceilings.
- **After:** the same tasks routed by Tally.
- **Repeats:** two of each, three if time allows. Each run starts from the same commit.
- **Reported:** cost per merged PR, pass rate, total cost, and the spread. Every run is published, including any Tally loses.
- **Size:** 28 task runs, three at a time, roughly three to four hours including setup per worker.

## 9. Acceptance checks

Run in this order. Do not start a check until the one before it passes.

| # | Check | Pass when |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | `npm test`, typecheck, build | All clean on `main`. |
| T2 | `tally demo` and `tally demo --live` | Seven tasks; one stopped and recovered; the live variant shows all three products on with honest status. |
| T3 | One real task | PR opened, tests decide, ledger row real, trace in neatlogs, checkpoint in Entire, spend in cfo.ai. |
| T4 | Forced failure | Stopped at the ceiling, continued by a stronger model from the handoff, finished. |
| T5 | Budget too small | Tally completes what it can, marks the rest "not started: no budget", stays under budget. |
| T6 | Unsolvable task | Fails on both models, the run finishes the others. |
| T7 | Interrupted run | Resumes without redoing work or double counting. |
| T8 | Full run | Ledger total equals the sum of rows and equals cfo.ai. |
| T9 | Experiment | Both modes reported with spread; every number traceable to a neatlogs trace. |
| T10 | Stranger install | A person who has not seen the code completes one task on a second repository using only the README. |
| T11 | Products off | Each of the three off in turn; the run completes and says so. |
| T12 | Hosted page | Public URL loads on a phone, shows the final runs, exposes no keys. |

## 10. What only you can do

| Needed | For | Needed before |
|---|---|---|
| Go-ahead for the first real run on fly-doom-jev | B1, and everything after it | Anything else |
| Approve the Codex hooks (`/hooks` in Codex) | E4: without it Entire has no worker sessions | B1 |
| Say yes or no to installing the neatlogs worker hooks, which edit `~/.claude` and `~/.codex` | N2 | N2 |
| Go-ahead to file the seven issues on fly-doom-jev | Intake from GitHub issues; the YAML file works without it | The full seven-task run |
| Decide where the gateway key may live: in an AO project's settings, or behind a small local proxy Tally runs | B6: real per-token billing in the ledger. Without it, cost is tokens times list price on subscription models, and the video says so. | B6 |
| A neatlogs service-account token and project id | N3 | N3 |
| Your pricing assumptions for the business plan | C5 | C5 |
| Go-ahead to create public AWS resources, and install the AWS CLI | H1, H2 | H1 |
| #neatHack posts, and recording the video | 15% and 20% of the score | Submission |

## 11. Risks, and what gets cut first

- **Time.** The list is long for the time left before the 12 Oct, 23:55 IST deadline. If it slips, cut in this order: Slack alert (not planned above), E6, C4, F8, B9's wizard prompts (keep a hand-written `tally.yaml`), a third repeat, N3 (keep the local history file), H3. Never cut B1, B2, the baseline comparison, or the evidence links: each is named evidence.
- **Subscription limits.** Lanes and real runs share the same Claude and Codex plans. A limit hit mid-experiment pauses workers. The gateway tiers are the relief, which is why that decision matters.
- **Routing may save less than hoped.** The 20% cap bounds the loss per task. The result is published either way.
- **The failure scene may not happen by itself.** B2 produces it on purpose, and the video says so.
- **Entire handoff across models** worked once on a toy repository and has not been tried on a long session.
- **CrustData is untested.** If the API does not give a usable list, the market size in the plan is entered by hand and labelled as an estimate.
- **Environment setup per worker** on fly-doom-jev may dominate small tasks. B3 keeps it out of the ceiling, but it still costs wall-clock time in the experiment.

# Tally: implementation plan for the final version

Written 10 Oct 2026, 21:05 IST, updated 21:20 IST against `main` at `7f37c0e`. Submission closes 12 Oct, 23:55 IST. This plan replaces sections 2 and 5 to 8 of the first plan (`neatlogs-hack-1/tally-implementation-plan.md`); the product idea and the routing rule in that plan still stand.

Everything in this document is still to be built unless it is listed under "Built" in section 1.

## 1. Where we start from

### Built and on `main` (19 PRs merged, 184 tests passing)

- **One run loop.** Intake, sizing, routing, ceiling watcher, test verification, one escalation, ledger. A dry run uses the same loop with only the worker faked.
- **CFO agent.** Sizer, price history with a no-data prior, routing rule with budget check and a one-sentence reason, ceiling watcher, escalation, baseline mode.
- **Adapters.** Agent Orchestrator (spawn, poll, usage, kill), GitHub issue intake with a YAML fallback, test verifier, neatlogs trace, entire-graph sizing, file price history, cfo.ai budget.
- **CLI.** `tally run` (`--dry-run`, `--plan`, `--only`, `--budget`, `--baseline`), `tally demo` (and `--live`, with all three products on and no real workers), `tally dashboard`, `tally doctor`, `tally login cfoai`.
- **Dashboard.** Static page: budget bar, integrations strip, Tasks (one row per piece of work), Ledger (one row per paid attempt), sample and replay modes.
- **Accounts.** neatlogs key set, Entire logged in with the repo copied to project `neatlogs-hack`, cfo.ai logged in with a budget table that Tally has read live ($40 for October).

### Not yet true

- **No real worker has ever run.** Every cost seen so far is simulated. This is the last piece of V1 and it needs your go-ahead.
- **cfo.ai write-back** has only been tested against a fake server.
- **Ledger rows have a neatlogs trace id but no clickable link.** The address format of a trace in the neatlogs dashboard has not been verified.
- **Entire records none of the Codex workers.** Their hooks are waiting for your approval (`/hooks` in Codex).
- **neatlogs sees decisions, not worker sessions.** The worker hook packages are not installed.
- **The cheap-tier threshold (0.65) is fitted to the sample backlog**, not measured.

## 2. What the final version is

A judge can do three things, and each one works without help:

1. Open a public dashboard and see real recorded runs: what each task cost, why it went to that model, what was stopped, what was escalated, and how the total compares with sending everything to the top model.
2. Run `tally demo` on their own machine with no accounts and watch the full loop in two minutes.
3. Run `tally init` in their own repository and have Tally drive their agents on their issues.

Behind that sits one backend, used by all three, and five outside products that each make a decision possible at run time.

| Judged on | Weight | What the final version shows |
|---|---|---|
| The agent | 30% | Real runs on a real backlog, measured against a baseline, with a stopped runaway and a recovered failure. |
| Use of neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai | 25% | Each product changes a decision during the run (section 4), and the dashboard links to the evidence. |
| Demo video | 20% | The dashboard tells the story on real data. |
| Building in public | 15% | #neatHack posts with dashboard screenshots and real numbers. |
| Usefulness and originality | 10% | "They cap people, we cap tasks", backed by the experiment and a business plan in cfo.ai. |

## 3. Backend

| # | Work | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | **First real run.** Register fly-doom-jev as an AO project, run one task with a small budget. | A worker opens a PR, the tests decide the result, one ledger row has real tokens and cost. |
| B2 | **Forced failure and handoff.** Run one medium task with a ceiling set far too low. | The worker is stopped at the ceiling, and a stronger model continues on the same branch from the handoff summary and finishes. |
| B3 | **Worker setup per task.** Each worker checkout needs `make setup` (about a minute, 450 MB). Run it before the worker starts and keep its cost out of the task's ceiling. | A real task does not fail or get stopped because of environment setup. |
| B4 | **Concurrency.** Up to three workers at once, with the budget check done before each spawn so parallel tasks cannot overspend together. | A seven-task run with three in flight never exceeds the budget. |
| B5 | **Resume and partial failure.** Kill Tally mid-run and restart. | No finished task is redone and no cost is counted twice, including while workers are still alive. |
| B6 | **Model tiers.** Subscription tiers through `ao spawn` by default. Gateway tiers (paid per token) if you approve where the key lives (section 10). | `tally.yaml` can mix both, and every tier's cost is tokens times list price. |

---
name: using-ao
description: "Catalog of the AO (Agent Orchestrator) `ao` CLI: spawning workers, managing sessions and projects, creating reusable Cues, sending messages, controlling the shared browser, previewing pages, and daemon control. Use when using the ao CLI, creating Cues, spawning workers, or managing AO sessions in an AO workspace."
trigger: "Using the ao CLI in an AO workspace: creating Cues, spawning workers, managing sessions/projects, sending messages, controlling or previewing pages."
---

# AO CLI Catalog

`ao` is a thin CLI over the local AO daemon. Every command is `ao <command> --help` for the authoritative flag list.

| Command | What it does | When to use | Details |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spawn` | Spawn a project worker, orchestrator, or projectless standalone worker | Starting a new task or issue | [commands/spawn.md](commands/spawn.md) |
| `session` | Manage agent sessions (list, kill, rename, restore, etc.) | Inspecting or controlling running/terminated sessions | [commands/session.md](commands/session.md) |
| `agent` | Inspect installed harnesses and launch readiness | Choosing or diagnosing an agent harness | `ao agent ls --refresh` |
| `pr` | Merge a PR or resolve its review threads | Completing a reviewed change | `ao pr merge` / `ao pr resolve-comments` |
| `project` | Register, inspect, configure, or remove projects | Setting up or managing repos AO knows about | [commands/project.md](commands/project.md) |
| `automation` | Manage durable recurring session automations | Creating, editing, disabling, deleting, and inspecting scheduled runs | [commands/automation.md](commands/automation.md) |
| `cue` | Create or list reusable project Cues | Saving a repetitive command or agent task at the user's request | [commands/cue.md](commands/cue.md) |
| `orchestrator` | List orchestrator sessions | Viewing which sessions are orchestrators | [commands/orchestrator.md](commands/orchestrator.md) |
| `review` | Start, list, cancel, or submit AO's native reviewer for a worker's PR (default: this session) | Getting an adversarial review of an AO session's PR; never spawn a worker to review | [commands/review.md](commands/review.md) |
| `send` | Send a message to a running agent session | Correcting or directing a live agent | [commands/send.md](commands/send.md) |
| `report` | Persist a meaningful worker report | Checkpoints, blockers, decisions, outputs, and completion | [commands/report.md](commands/report.md) |
| `preview` | Start a session-owned app or open an exact URL/file | Running and showing the worker's relevant app, Markdown, HTML, PDF, or image | [commands/preview.md](commands/preview.md) |
| `render` | Show a self-contained HTML page inline in a chat thread | Answering with a chart, table, diagram, or mockup | [commands/render.md](commands/render.md) |
| `browser` | Inspect and control the session's shared live browser | Verifying a web app through snapshots, interactions, waits, screenshots, console, and errors | [commands/browser.md](commands/browser.md) |
| `start` | Fetch (if needed) and open the AO desktop app | Launching the app | [commands/start.md](commands/start.md) |
| `stop` | Stop the AO daemon | Shutting down AO | [commands/stop.md](commands/stop.md) |
| `status` | Show daemon status | Verifying the daemon is up and healthy | [commands/status.md](commands/status.md) |
| `doctor` | Run local health checks | Diagnosing AO setup problems | [commands/doctor.md](commands/doctor.md) |
| `import` | Import projects from a legacy AO install | Migrating from the old flat-file store | [commands/import.md](commands/import.md) |
| `version` | Print version information | Checking installed version | - |
| `completion` | Generate shell completion scripts | Setting up tab completion | - |

## Conventions

- Most read commands accept `--json` for machine-readable output.
- `-p / --project` scopes session subcommand lookups to one project.
- Session and project ids are shown by `ao session ls` and `ao project ls`.
- To refer to a session in AO Chat or the AO terminal, use the canonical in-app
  link `ao://sessions/{project-id}/{session-id}`. Read
  [commands/session.md](commands/session.md) for identity, encoding, and safety
  rules before constructing one.
- When the user asks to save a repeatable task as a Cue, use `ao cue list --json` to check existing definitions, then `ao cue create`. An agent Cue stores a reusable instruction; a command Cue stores an exact shell command. This agent-facing command can create and read Cues, but cannot edit or delete them. Direct the user to project settings for changes to existing Cues.
- `--agent` is an alias for `--harness` on `ao spawn`.
- Every command accepts `-h / --help` for the full flag list.
- For frontend launch, preview selection, or artifact handoff, read
  [commands/preview.md](commands/preview.md) before acting. Its static-file,
  project-runtime, and automatic-handoff rules are load-bearing.
- For page inspection, interaction, or request diagnosis, read
  [commands/browser.md](commands/browser.md). It defines shared-tab behavior
  and the opt-in network policy.

Use [references.md](references.md) only when a natural-language request does
not map clearly to a command above.

# ao report

Persist a meaningful worker report for durable delivery to the active project
orchestrator.

## Syntax

```text
ao report <free-form-text>
ao report --checkpoint --note <text> [output flags]
ao report --needs-input --note <text> [output flags]
ao report --stuck --note <text> [output flags]
ao report --done --note <text> [output flags]
```

Output flags are repeatable:

```text
--artifact <opaque-reference>
--pr-created <pr-or-mr-url>
--pr-reviewed <pr-or-mr-url>
```

Use reports for meaningful transitions, decisions, blockers, required input,
outputs, and terminal judgment. Do not narrate routine commands. Outputs do not
imply completion, and `--done` does not terminate the session.

Attach a reviewable deliverable as soon as it is ready, not only at `--done`:
use `--artifact <reference>` on the report for the milestone that produced it.
Examples include a requested document, a rendered dashboard, or another output
the orchestrator or human needs to open directly. `--artifact` takes any opaque
reference string; it is not validated as a URL.
In a chat session, an HTML file from the artifact directory that you attach
with `--artifact` also shows in the thread.

Routine test logs, command output, scratch notes, and intermediate diagnostics
are working material, not deliverables. Do not attach them unless requested or
needed to explain an actionable failure. Summarize validation in the report note;
when a separate deliverable is useful, prefer one consolidated report over
individual logs. Ordinary progress updates and concise final answers do not
need separate artifact files.

Saving a local artifact or attaching its reference to an AO report is not
external publishing authorization. Publish externally only within the
user-authorized scope.

`--pr-created` and `--pr-reviewed` accept complete GitHub PR or GitLab MR URLs.

`--needs-input` requests immediate non-interrupting delivery. `--stuck`
requests immediate delivery plus a rate-limited interrupt. Informational work
batches for up to one hour, while the first done report opens a fixed five
minute settlement window.

**Examples:**

```bash
ao report "The focused tests pass; I am checking the generated diff."
ao report --done --note "Ready for review." \
  --pr-created https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/88
```

content.text: I’ve found the current B7 gap: routing still uses a fixed `cheapConfidence: 0.65`, and history is always blended with the prior even when real observations exist. I’m going to make routing pick between observed stats and prior explicitly, with a minimum sample count, and compute the confidence needed from the same expected-cost inequality instead of a hand-tuned constant.

I’ve found the current B7 gap: routing still uses a fixed `cheapConfidence: 0.65`, and history is always blended with the prior even when real observations exist. I’m going to make routing pick between observed stats and prior explicitly, with a minimum sample count, and compute the confidence needed from the same expected-cost inequality instead of a hand-tuned constant.

The existing `history.ts` blend still has value for baseline estimates, so I’m keeping it intact. The router itself will now decide whether a history cell is usable, and its sentence will name either “using prior” or “history changed the choice” when that is what happened.

# CrustData D1 spike findings

Date: 2026-10-10
Scope: read-only API probing with `CRUSTDATA_API_KEY` from `~/.tally/.env`. The key was not printed or copied.

## Documentation checked

- CrustData documents `POST https://api.crustdata.com/company/search` with `Authorization: Bearer ...`, `content-type: application/json`, and `x-api-version: 2025-11-01`.
- Public docs say Company Search returns `companies`, `next_cursor`, and `total_count`, and prices search at `0.03 credits per result` on the product page. The live response headers reported higher per-call credit figures for this account/path; see below.
- Docs/product pages say Company Search supports firmographic, headcount, hiring, job-listing, employee-skill and keyword style filters, but the live API rejected some advertised fields as conditions.

Sources:
- https://crustdata.com/company-data-api
- https://crustdata.com/apis/company-discovery
- https://www.crustdata.com/blog/company-search-api

## Calls made

All calls used `POST /company/search`, `x-api-version: 2025-11-01`, and tiny `limit` values.

1. Basic company search, valid

Payload shape:

```json
{
  "filters": {
    "op": "and",
    "conditions": [
      { "field": "headcount.total", "type": ">", "value": 50 }
    ]
  },
  "fields": ["basic_info.name", "basic_info.primary_domain", "headcount.total"],
  "limit": 1
}
```

Result:

- HTTP 200.
- Top-level keys: `companies`, `next_cursor`, `total_count`.
- Example returned company: `a2z Infrastructure (P) Ltd`, domain `a2zgroup.co.in`, headcount `321`.
- `total_count`: `994745`.
- Response header `x-credit-cost`: `0.43`.

2. Basic company search with hiring fields returned, valid

Payload shape:

```json
{
  "filters": {
    "op": "and",
    "conditions": [
      { "field": "headcount.total", "type": "=>", "value": 51 },
      { "field": "headcount.total", "type": "=<", "value": 500 }
    ]
  },
  "fields": [
    "basic_info.name",
    "basic_info.primary_domain",
    "basic_info.description",
    "headcount.total",
    "hiring.openings_count",
    "hiring.by_function_6m_pct.engineering",
    "taxonomy.professional_network_industry"
  ],
  "limit": 1
}
```

Result:

- HTTP 200.
- Same company came back because the filter is broad.
- `hiring` was `null` for that company, but the fields were accepted as return fields.
- `taxonomy.professional_network_industry` returned `Oil and Gas`.
- `total_count`: `891820`.
- Response header `x-credit-cost`: `0.53`.

3. Invalid/zero-credit probes

The API returned useful validation errors and reported `x-credit-cost: 0` for these rejected requests:

- `taxonomy.industry` is not a valid return field. The API suggested `taxonomy` or `taxonomy.professional_network_industry`.
- `between` is not a valid comparison operator in the live endpoint despite examples using it. The API accepts `=>` and `=<` for lower/upper bounds.
- `query` is a return field but is not supported as a filter condition.
- `hiring.openings_count` and `hiring.by_function_6m_pct.engineering` are accepted as return fields but were rejected as condition fields in this endpoint/account.
- A guessed `company_keywords` condition did not get a fair test because the request also had the invalid taxonomy return field; I did not spend another call after the stricter field errors were clear.

## Can we list engineering teams adopting coding agents?

Not directly from this spike alone.

What works:

- Company Search can return structured company lists with domains, descriptions, headcount, taxonomy and selected hiring fields.
- The API exposes an `available_fields` list in validation metadata that includes hiring fields such as `hiring.openings_count`, `hiring.by_function_6m_pct.engineering`, and `hiring.by_function_qoq_pct.engineering`.
- A D2 implementation can reliably save and rerun exact structured company-search payloads.

What did not work in the live probes:

- Free-text `query` could not be used as a condition.
- Engineering hiring fields could not be used as conditions in `POST /company/search`; they appear returnable but not filterable through this endpoint/account.
- I did not find a confirmed condition field for “uses Cursor/Copilot/Codex/coding agents” without either docs for keyword filters or an enrichment/search endpoint that accepts natural-language queries.

Likely D2 path:

1. Use `/company/search` for the structured company universe: e.g. headcount range, country, software/technology taxonomy where valid, and return `basic_info.description`, `hiring.*`, `taxonomy.*`.
2. For “adopting coding agents,” add a second stage if available: either CrustData MCP/natural-language search, a realtime search endpoint that accepts keyword filters, or enrichment fields/posts/jobs that can be searched for terms like `Cursor`, `GitHub Copilot`, `Codex`, `AI coding assistant`, `developer productivity`, and `agentic coding`.
3. Until a keyword/natural-language condition is verified, label D2 as “companies with engineering/hiring signals plus coding-agent keyword evidence” only when that evidence comes from a returned text field or a separate verified endpoint.

## Credit cost observed

- Successful returned-row calls: `0.43 + 0.53 = 0.96` credits by response header.
- Rejected validation calls: `0` credits by response header.
- This differs from the public product page statement of `0.03 credits per result`, so D2 should record response headers for actual cost accounting.

Usage:
  entire graph <command> [flags]

Set up your agent:
  init-agents      Install the coding-agent guide into AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md
  agent-guide      Print the coding-agent operating guide
  index            Build/warm a committed-tree cache variant for matching queries
  capabilities     List parsed languages, relation types, and features

Inspect the graph:
  search           Find the code for a task from a plain-language query (start here)
  neighbors        Who calls this / what does it call (targeted relations)
  impact           One-shot blast radius for changing a symbol
  def              What a name IS: declaration, fields, and method surface
  explain          Resolve symbols named by a failing build or test
  symbols          Stream every symbol definition (bulk NDJSON)
  edges            Stream every relation (bulk NDJSON)
  snapshot         Stream the whole graph: files, symbols, and relations (bulk NDJSON)
  snapshot-query   Query a compact snapshot without rebuilding the graph

Analyze changes & more:
  commit           Entity-level change list for a commit vs its first parent
  diff             Entity-level change list between two refs
  checkpoint       Analyze the commit behind an Entire-Checkpoint trailer
  verify           Run a test command and return an adjudicated verdict, not test output
  stats            Human report: graph usage vs grep/read, and estimated token savings

Help & diagnostics:

  doctor           Diagnose the environment and confirm no-egress
  version          Print the plugin version (and provider name with --json)

item.stdout:
Run a test command and return an adjudicated verdict, not test output

Usage:
  entire graph verify --test "<cmd>" --repo . [--setup "<cmd>"] [--record-baseline path | --pre-edit-baseline path] [--max-bytes 2048]

verify runs your test command and reports WHICH TESTS CHANGED rather than what the runner printed: which newly pass, which newly fail, and which were ALREADY failing before the edit (labelled PRE-EXISTING). Raw runner output is never forwarded — ids are, text is not — and id lists cap at 20 with a count.

Record a baseline on the pristine tree first (--record-baseline), then pass that file as --pre-edit-baseline after editing. Without a baseline the verdict is a state rather than a delta, so a failure that predates the change cannot be labelled as one.

Parsers: pytest, jest/vitest, cargo test, go test, phpunit, rspec, minitest, maven/gradle surefire, ctest. An unrecognised format degrades to an exit-code-only verdict and says so.

Flags:
  --test <cmd>                 The test command to run (required)
  --repo <path>                Repository to run in (default: current repo)
  --setup <cmd>                Command run before the tests; its output never contributes test ids
  --record-baseline <path>     Write the pristine-tree result to this file instead of adjudicating
  --pre-edit-baseline <path>   Diff this run against a previously recorded baseline
  --max-bytes <n>              Cap the rendered verdict; the verdict clause always survives (default: 2048)

Examples:
  entire graph verify --repo . --test "pytest tests/test_parser.py" --record-baseline /tmp/base.json
  entire graph verify --repo . --test "pytest tests/test_parser.py" --pre-edit-baseline /tmp/base.json

Run a test command and return an adjudicated verdict, not test output

Usage:
  entire graph verify --test "<cmd>" --repo . [--setup "<cmd>"] [--record-baseline path | --pre-edit-baseline path] [--max-bytes 2048]

verify runs your test command and reports WHICH TESTS CHANGED rather than what the runner printed: which newly pass, which newly fail, and which were ALREADY failing before the edit (labelled PRE-EXISTING). Raw runner output is never forwarded — ids are, text is not — and id lists cap at 20 with a count.

Record a baseline on the pristine tree first (--record-baseline), then pass that file as --pre-edit-baseline after editing. Without a baseline the verdict is a state rather than a delta, so a failure that predates the change cannot be labelled as one.

Parsers: pytest, jest/vitest, cargo test, go test, phpunit, rspec, minitest, maven/gradle surefire, ctest. An unrecognised format degrades to an exit-code-only verdict and says so.

Flags:
  --test <cmd>                 The test command to run (required)
  --repo <path>                Repository to run in (default: current repo)
  --setup <cmd>                Command run before the tests; its output never contributes test ids
  --record-baseline <path>     Write the pristine-tree result to this file instead of adjudicating
  --pre-edit-baseline <path>   Diff this run against a previously recorded baseline
  --max-bytes <n>              Cap the rendered verdict; the verdict clause always survives (default: 2048)

- Missing/blocked: If a named skill isn't in the list or the path can't be read, say so briefly and continue with the best fallback.
- How to use a skill (progressive disclosure):
  1) After deciding to use a skill, the main agent must expand the listed short `path` with the matching alias from `### Skill roots`, then open and read its `SKILL.md` completely before taking task actions. If a read is truncated or paginated, continue until EOF.
  2) When `SKILL.md` references relative paths (e.g., `scripts/foo.py`), resolve them relative to the directory containing that expanded `SKILL.md` first, and only consider other paths if needed.
  3) If `SKILL.md` points to extra folders such as `references/`, use its routing instructions to identify the files required for the task. The main agent must read each required instruction or reference file itself before acting on it. Do not delegate reading, summarizing, or interpreting skill instructions to a subagent. Subagents may still perform task work when the selected skill allows it.
  4) If `scripts/` exist, prefer running or patching them instead of retyping large code blocks.
  5) If `assets/` or templates exist, reuse them instead of recreating from scratch.
